heading: Which part of the Ecuadorian Amazon should I choose?
intro: Start with the proposed experience and the complete journey from your departure point. Compare a stay around Cuyabeno or Yasuní and the Napo corridor with the options described for Tena, Misahuallí and Puyo. These guides introduce regional choices; they do not establish what a specific provider offers. Ask for the accommodation location, excursion setting and transfer plan before treating two itineraries as equivalent.
points: Choose the interests that matter most to your group.
Compare one coherent regional base at a time.
Confirm the exact property and excursion locations.

heading: How many days do I need?
intro: There is no single duration that fits every group. Read the daily schedule, count nights and check the time remaining after arrival and departure transfers. A shorter stay may suit one set of priorities while another needs more unhurried observation time. Compare the proposed three-, four- and five-day structures through their actual activities rather than assuming the headline number describes full days in the forest.
points: Separate days, nights and full activity periods.
Leave room for rest and your onward plans.
Ask which activities are essential to your interests.

heading: How will I reach the accommodation?
intro: The provider’s written plan should connect your actual starting point with the base and the return journey. Ask which road or river segments are proposed, who arranges them, where you meet and what is included. Do not choose a connection from a photograph or a broad regional description. Confirm the timing for your dates and ask how a change would affect the rest of the itinerary.
points: Request the complete outward and return sequence.
Clarify meeting points and responsible contacts.
Check luggage arrangements with the actual provider.

heading: Will the activities suit our group?
intro: Describe your group before choosing the program: ages, mobility, balance, interests, walking preferences and any requirements the provider needs to assess. Ask about the actual terrain, boarding and pace of each outing. A family label or a comfortable-looking room cannot confirm suitability. Request specific arrangements and alternatives in writing, and keep any unanswered requirement visible while comparing the proposals.
points: Discuss physical demands rather than destination labels.
Ask how shared activities and guiding work.
Confirm any agreed assistance for your booking.

heading: What equipment and guiding are included?
intro: Inclusions depend on the written proposal. Ask what equipment is supplied, shared or required, and discuss what you plan to carry. Confirm the guiding language, group arrangement and experience relevant to your interests. If bird observation or photography is important, explain that in your inquiry. A gallery can introduce an interest, but it does not establish equipment provision, specialist guiding or a guaranteed sighting.
points: Confirm supplied equipment and your own packing list.
Ask who guides the proposed activities and in which language.
Treat wildlife photographs as documented examples.

heading: What should I clarify before booking?
intro: Request the dated itinerary, complete price, included services, exclusions and written change terms together. Confirm who receives the inquiry and who operates the journey; this guide does not itself confirm availability or a reservation. Review current official advice for each gateway and route. Resolve the questions that affect your decision before accepting the final proposal, and keep the agreed documents accessible during planning.
points: Confirm dates and availability directly with the provider.
Read payment, modification and cancellation terms.
Save the final itinerary and contact details together.
